name: Greenwich Park & Blackheath
highlights: The oldest Royal Park, home to the Prime Meridian and Royal Observatory, with three city-view hills and the open expanse of Blackheath.

name: Sutcliffe Park
highlights: A compact wetland park with a running track and figure-of-eight trails ideal for pacing reps.

name: Danson Park
highlights: One of London's top suburban parks, circling a large boating lake past a grand Georgian mansion.

name: Scadbury Park
highlights: An easy-to-follow woodland-and-meadow nature reserve loop past the moated ruins of Scadbury manor.

name: Petts Wood
highlights: A rolling four-mile loop mixing ancient woods, heath and farmland with lung-pumping views.

name: Jubilee Country Park
highlights: A flat figure-of-eight through woods and wildflower meadows that bloom in spring and summer.

name: High Elms Country Park
highlights: An undulating woodland-and-formal-garden nature reserve loop that can extend to Charles Darwin's Down House.

name: The Woods of Croydon
highlights: Links Croydon's spider's web of woodland commons along the fourth section of the way-marked London LOOP.

name: South Norwood Country Park
highlights: A rejuvenated nature reserve of grassland and wetland beside the Croydon Arena athletics track.

name: Crystal Palace Park
highlights: A hilly historic park with Victorian dinosaur sculptures, a landmark BBC transmitter and a national athletics stadium.

name: Peckham Rye & Nunhead Cemetery
highlights: Pairs a flat sports-field park-and-common circuit with the atmospheric Victorian Nunhead Cemetery.

name: Waterlink Way
highlights: A flat, well-signed waterway trail following the Ravensbourne and Pool rivers from Sydenham north to the Thames near Greenwich.

name: Three Commons
highlights: An expertly way-marked loop weaving through three superb suburban commons and woods around Hayes and Keston.

name: Cray Riverway
highlights: A long way-marked riverway through marshland and woods tracing the banks of the Thames, Darent and Cray.

name: Lesnes Abbey & Thamesmead
highlights: An 8.7mi Green Chain loop linking the 12th-century Lesnes Abbey ruins, Southmere Lake and the industrial Thames Path.

name: Oxleas Woods & Shooters Hill
highlights: An incredible array of hilly Green Chain green spaces from the Thames Barrier up to Shooters Hill and Severndroog Castle.

name: Eltham & Avery Hill
highlights: A Green Chain figure-of-eight past open parkland, woods, a palace and the quaint lakeside Tarn.

name: Beckenham Place & Elmstead
highlights: A hilly Green Chain figure-of-eight through ancient woods, rolling suburbs and the tranquil Durham Woodland Walk.

name: Crystal Palace to Nunhead
highlights: A point-to-point over south London's hills linking a historic park, ancient woods and Victorian cemeteries.
